statement: The function returns a result r such that vals(r) = [ vals(head)[i] | 0 <= i < len(head) and occ(vals(head)[i], head) = 1 ], where the sequence is taken in increasing order of i. Equivalently, vals(r) is obtained from vals(head) by deleting every occurrence of every value that occurs more than once in head, and keeping the remaining elements in their original relative order.
preconditions: head is a linked list whose value sequence vals(head) is non-decreasing: for every i with 0 <= i < len(head)-1, vals(head)[i] <= vals(head)[i+1]; and every value satisfies -100 <= vals(head)[i] <= 100 for 0 <= i < len(head).

statement: The function returns a result r with len(r) <= len(head).
preconditions: head is a sorted (non-decreasing) linked list with all values in [-100, 100].

statement: For every such head the function returns a result r; it never fails, panics, reads out of bounds, or overflows.
preconditions: head is a sorted (non-decreasing) linked list with all values in [-100, 100].

statement: The returned list r is sorted non-decreasing: for every i with 0 <= i < len(r)-1, vals(r)[i] <= vals(r)[i+1].
preconditions: head is a sorted (non-decreasing) linked list with all values in [-100, 100].

statement: The returned list r contains no repeated value: for every i, j with 0 <= i < j < len(r), vals(r)[i] != vals(r)[j]. (Equivalently, given S4, vals(r) is strictly increasing.)
preconditions: head is a sorted (non-decreasing) linked list with all values in [-100, 100].

statement: For every i with 0 <= i < len(r), occ(vals(r)[i], head) = 1: every value that appears in the returned list r occurs exactly once in head.
preconditions: head is a sorted (non-decreasing) linked list with all values in [-100, 100].

statement: For every integer v, if occ(v, head) = 1 then occ(v, r) = 1: every value that occurs exactly once in head appears exactly once in the returned list r.
preconditions: head is a sorted (non-decreasing) linked list with all values in [-100, 100].

statement: For every integer v, if occ(v, head) >= 2 then occ(v, r) = 0: every value that occurs more than once in head is completely removed from the returned list r.
preconditions: head is a sorted (non-decreasing) linked list with all values in [-100, 100].

statement: vals(r) is a subsequence of vals(head): there exist indices 0 <= i_0 < i_1 < ... < i_{len(r)-1} < len(head) such that vals(r)[k] = vals(head)[i_k] for every k with 0 <= k < len(r). (The condition is vacuous when len(r) = 0.)
preconditions: head is a sorted (non-decreasing) linked list with all values in [-100, 100].

statement: len(r) = the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(head) and occ(vals(head)[i], head) = 1: the length of r equals the number of positions in head whose value occurs exactly once in head.
preconditions: head is a sorted (non-decreasing) linked list with all values in [-100, 100].

statement: If len(head) = 0 then len(r) = 0 (r is Nil).
preconditions: head is a sorted (non-decreasing) linked list with all values in [-100, 100].

statement: If len(head) = 1 then len(r) = 1 and vals(r)[0] = vals(head)[0].
preconditions: head is a sorted (non-decreasing) linked list with all values in [-100, 100].

statement: If every value of head occurs exactly once in head (i.e., for every i with 0 <= i < len(head), occ(vals(head)[i], head) = 1), then vals(r) = vals(head).
preconditions: head is a sorted (non-decreasing) linked list with all values in [-100, 100].

statement: len(r) = 0 if and only if for every i with 0 <= i < len(head), occ(vals(head)[i], head) >= 2. Equivalently, the returned list is empty exactly when head is empty or every value of head is repeated.
preconditions: head is a sorted (non-decreasing) linked list with all values in [-100, 100].
